Environmental Ed Day 9 Marsh Dash

Oct 14, 2010 • Janice Cotcher

The dreaded day of the bike trip arrived and it wasn’t as bad as I thought it would be.

I decided to take my parents’ van and park it far away from the university so I didn’t have to pay for parking. It also gave me a chance to practice riding the bike a bit more before the day’s trip. Ideally I would have liked to ride to school from home but I live too far away and am too out of shape. If I rode my bike to school there would be no way I’d be able to ride it around the lake then back home again.

Overall the trip to the university went well except it was a bit of a pain to shoulder check over the hood of my jacket. It was also difficult to turn left once because cars in my lane kept on passing me. I had to keep an eye on what was going on in front of me and behind me just to turn. I definitely have new found sympathy for people who ride their bikes all the time. Fact: people who drive cars are jerks to cyclists.

There were several people from my class already waiting when I arrived. Talking to my classmates I realized that other people had the same anxieties that I did so it made me feel a little better.

Turned out the plan for the morning was a Marsh Dash. Every year the Friends of Wascana Marsh host a scavenger hunt for teams of runners called the Marsh Dash. It is a way to promote people to notice nature as they run. This is a pretty neat idea. Often as I walked along these same trails, I thought it was such a shame that runners don’t even seem to notice the beauty that is around them. Due to time constraints and lack of physical fitness, our class did the Marsh Dash on our bikes.

Some highlights from the trip:

My group on top of the tallest hill in the park. The clue was

What has roots as nobody sees, Is taller than trees Up, up it goes, And yet never grows? - J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit

! As you can clearly see, I am the giant of group.

Canada Geese and Mallards! ! If you couldn’t tell by now, I like birds. We got a little distracted from our scavenger hunt because we saw a muskrat in the water. He/she went under water and I was taking pictures while we waited for he/she to resurface. Unfortunately the muskrat disappeared, I never got my picture but it was still neat to see it.

This brings me to an important point: give students focus when they are on a field trip. Seeing the muskrat would have not been possible if I was not in that exact spot because of the scavenger hunt. I was forced into parts of the park that I’ve never been to before and was rewarded by seeing wildlife I didn’t even know was in the park. This sighting got my group talking about the pelicans in the park and made me want to go exploring to find them. People like me don’t need structure to be motivated to enjoy nature but I’m sure there are many in my class that do. I think activities like the Marsh Dash are great for inspiring people to notice their surroundings more often.

Finally, my favorite picture of the day ! I thought it was a crane but now I’m not sure. The reason the picture is so close is because the bird has an injured wing and is recuperating at the display ponds.
